evaluation: Rolling-origin (expanding window) evaluation on train.csv, refitting the full pipeline on all earlier data each time (training targets end before the test block, 1 h gap, so no label leakage): 3 blocks 27 Mar-17 Apr, 17 Apr-8 May, 8 May-1 Jun gave RMSE 44.8 / 40.3 / 26.5 ppm (pooled 37.5) vs persistence of the 1 h-old value 46.4 / 48.0 / 28.5 (pooled 41.3), i.e. about 9% better; ~8 model/feature variants were compared on the same blocks so the pooled figure is slightly optimistic, and error scales with how much weekday occupancy there is (blocks range 26-45 ppm), so I quote 35 ppm with a plausible range of 25-45; a quiet summer/holiday period would give much less (about 10-20 ppm). predict() was also checked mechanically: truncating the file, and overwriting all data after a time T0 with random rows, leaves forecasts for every interval <= T0+45 min bit-for-bit unchanged. bemlops' own fit() on its last-15% test window (late May) reported persistence 29.5 ppm and no ML model beating it.
data_findings: Raw 5-min export, 27,204 rows, 2023-02-27 to 2023-05-31, 22 columns, ';' separator, UTF-8 BOM, '#N/A' for missing, timestamps with UTC offsets (+0100 -> +0200 at the 2023-03-26 DST change). (1) Row order/duplicates: a 288-row block (2023-05-24 23:05 to 2023-05-25 23:00) is logged twice (identical values); a 30-row block on 2023-04-24 (15:30 back to 13:05) is in reverse order and actually fills a 2.5 h hole; a 12 h gap on 2023-04-02 (07:40-19:45); the DST jump. Fixed by parsing to UTC, sorting, dropping exact duplicate timestamps, then working on a UTC grid and converting to local time only for calendar features and the output index. (2) RoomB CO2: 15 placeholders of -999 (masked), one isolated needle of 1521 ppm on 2023-04-21 (kept out of the inputs via a bin-median feature; cannot be predicted), and the point is change-of-value logged (95% of consecutive samples identical, steps of ~50 ppm, flat for up to 3.6 days when the room is empty), so long flat stretches are real and not a stuck sensor: they were NOT masked. The target is the mean of such held values, which makes it step-like and hard to forecast; the persistence baseline is therefore strong. (3) Room temperature changed unit from degC to degF at 2023-05-12 10:00 (values 70-83 until the end of the file): converted per sample (>45 means degF). (4) Outdoor temperature has 8 isolated spikes to 57-73 (glitches): masked (>35). Wind has 12 'OFFLINE' text values (-> NaN). (5) People__amount is only logged for 38% of the time (27 Feb-13 Apr and 30-31 May, flat 0 in between/NaN elsewhere), so it was NOT used (it would be missing in the future). The three setpoint/limit columns are constant and were dropped. Window open/closed changes only three times (8 May, 17 May, 23 May) so it is confounded with the period and was left out. (6) Regime change around 14-24 Apr: ventilation/damper behaviour and the Room__active pattern changed (weekday office-hour block afterwards, ad hoc bursts before), so training data is from two regimes. (7) Errors are concentrated on weekday afternoons (16-19 h) with sudden event-driven rises of 300-400 ppm within an hour that no 1 h-old information predicts; nights and weekends are easy (RMSE 10-20 ppm). Model inputs: bin means/median/last/min/max of the 15-min CO2, rolling CO2 stats, room occupancy flag (Room__active) and its history, ventilation airflow, damper, lights on/off, local time of day/weekday and the occupancy pattern of the previous 1-7 days at the same time. Outdoor temperature, solar, heating power, room temperature level and light level were excluded on purpose because with only 3 months of data they mostly encode 'season' and would extrapolate badly into summer. All lagged inputs are at least 4 bins (1 h) old; the target mean for interval T only uses 5-min samples with timestamps before T-45 min. predict() returns forecasts from the first interval in the file up to 1 h after the last complete 15-min bin (the live forecast); where no CO2 history exists (first hour of the file, long gaps) it falls back to the weekday/hour median from training.
usability: What worked: check_data caught most real problems on the raw frame (-999 CO2, the 1521 ppm needle, 'OFFLINE' text, unsorted rows, the 288 duplicated rows, the 12 h gap, the degF stretch in room temperature) and recognised the CO2/wind logging as change-of-value with a deadband (flat_ok=True worked once I used the dict form). Whole check/prepare/fit/save_run took ~80 s. Problems and gaps, all hit in this run: (1) Timestamps with mixed UTC offsets (this export has +0100 and +0200 because of DST) make Project(..., timestamp='timestamp', timestamp_format='%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z') raise a bare pandas 'ValueError: Mixed timezones detected. Pass utc=True...' (same with timestamp_format=None); schema.to_time_index does not use utc=True or convert to local time, so the user has to pre-parse; the skill's timestamp section covers UTC exports but not this common local-with-offset format, and the error is not wrapped with advice. (2) The room-temperature column switched from degC to degF on 12 May (21.8% of rows): check_data reports only 'out_of_range ... too many to be sensor glitches: check the declaration', with no date range, no hint that it is one contiguous stretch/unit change, and no unit_mismatch suggestion because most values fit degC. Declaring degF would make the other 78% wrong; there is no helper for per-segment unit conversion, so I converted per sample in my own loader. (3) The stuck-sensor rule is over-aggressive for sensors with a physical floor or COV logging: prepare() masked 9,759 of 26,916 (36%) solar-irradiance samples (the night-time floor of ~4 W/m2 repeated for 12 h) and 557 outdoor-temperature samples as 'stuck' with no deadband hint (the hint appeared for CO2 and wind but not for those), and silently forward-filled them up to 1 h; I had to know to declare flat_ok=True per column, and flat_ok is only available in the dict/ColumnSpec form (the shorthand string 'co2 [ppm]' cannot carry it and it is only described in the ColumnSpec docstring, not in SKILL.md). (4) The spring DST jump (01:55 -> 03:00) is merged into the 'gaps' warning (13 h 10 min = 12 h 5 min + 1 h 5 min) without saying it is the clock change. (5) fit() evaluates on one chronological test block (last ~15%, ~2 weeks, here late May): persistence RMSE was 29.5 ppm there but 46-48 ppm in April blocks, so a single block gives a very unstable headline number; there is no rolling-origin (multi-block) report even though TimeSeriesSplit is used internally for tuning. The ranking in that single window (persistence 26.3 > ridge 26.6 > gbm 29.7 on validation) says 'no ML beat persistence', whereas my own engineered features and an ExtraTrees delta model beat persistence by ~9% in a 3-block rolling-origin test (pooled 37.5 vs 41.3 ppm). (6) Feature engineering is limited to lags of declared columns (target lags 4-7 steps, 1 day, 1 week, 1-day mean) plus hour/dow: no rolling max/min, time-since-event, history-of-occupancy, bin median/last-value features and no hook for a custom estimator/feature builder, so the saved bemlops model could not be the final model; I would have to pre-compute those as 'other' columns and lose the guarantee that they are lag-safe (hard rule 2 then depends entirely on my code; I verified it with a truncation and a perturbation test instead). (7) The benchmark needs a forecast for intervals after the last timestamp in the file (live forecast) and an index per interval start; I could not tell from the docs whether ForecastModel.predict does exactly that for a file ending mid-interval, so I did not wrap it. (8) Not a bug but missing: no guidance in the skill on how to treat a People-counter that is only logged part of the time (I dropped it), and no 'regime change' check (the ventilation/occupancy regime changed ~14-24 Apr).
